articles.summary: The eight teams that are getting "Rivalries" uniforms for the 2026 NFL season are also featured in new Nike ads hyping up the jerseys.
articles.body:
The eight teams that are getting "Rivalries" uniforms for the 2026 NFL season are also featured in new Nike ads hyping up the jerseys.

This season will see the NFC North and AFC South get a new alternate jersey that will be used for a select game against a divisional opponent, like the NFC West and AFC East did last year..

Here are the Nike ads for each of the eight individual clubs.

Nike and the NFL formally unveiled the jerseys for the AFC South and NFC North earlier on Tuesday. The home team for each divisional matchup will wear the rivalries uniforms.

The Colts will be involved in three rivalries uniform games. They will wear theirs when they host the Houston Texans in Week 3, then the Texans will counter by wearing theirs when they host Indy in Week 11.

Jacksonville will wear its uniform against the Colts in Week 8. The Titans will showcase theirs when they host the Jaguars in Week 10.

The NFC North has an even split between the two teams, with the Packers and Bears designated rivals and Lions-Vikings designated rivals. Green Bay will show off its rivalries look against the Bears in Week 5, with Chicago doing so in Week 16.

Detroit will wear its jerseys in Week 8 against the Vikings, who will break out their rivalries uniforms vs. the Lions in Week 15.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Not Playing in Browns' Preseason Finale Explained by Todd Monken After QB1 Snub
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.

Monken also said that Deshaun Watson was the clear frontrunner for the starting position in the spring but Sanders made it a competition with his play over the summer.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Watson was officially, and somewhat shockingly , named the team's starter on Monday.

Neither Watson or Sanders were exactly brilliant during the first two preseason games:

But history suggests that Watson has little room for growth. Since joining the Browns in 2022 he's thrown for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns and 12 interceptions across 19 games, taking 70 sacks while completing 61.2 percent of his passes. The Browns are 9-10 in his starts.

Sanders is more of an unknown, though his rookie season was rough after he threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games (seven starts), taking 23 sacks while completing just 56.6 percent of his passes. The Browns went 3-4 in his starts.

One line of thinking is that the Browns probably should determine once and for all what they have in Sanders, especially since they have two first-round picks ahead of the 2027 draft, which is expected to have a strong quarterback class. It's hard to do that when he's sitting on the bench.

But Monken is a first-year head coach who wants to make a strong initial impression, and picking the veteran quarterback is normally the safer bet. The issue in this case is that Watson has never been good in Cleveland and was awful in his second preseason appearance. Choosing him as the starter certainly feels like a predetermined choice.

Regardless, the pecking order has been set. Nobody will be surprised if Sanders ultimately takes over as the starter at some point in the regular season, however.

articles.title: Chad Ochocinco points to Week 3 as Deshaun Watsonâs Browns future hangs in balance with Shedeur Sanders

He pointed specifically to the Brownsâ third game, saying a quarterback change could come before Week 4.Chad Ochocinco sets a Week 4 warning for Deshaun WatsonThe Browns will begin the 2026 regular season with Watson against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13.Cleveland then travels to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before returning home to play the Carolina Panthers in Week 3. That third game is the one Ochocinco believes could become a major test for Watson.Speaking on Nightcap, Ochocinco said he had already expected Watson to get the first chance because of his contract. The quarterback signed a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed deal with Cleveland in 2022, making the decision a major financial commitment for the Browns.âI said it before preseason started, when they went to training camp, itâs Deshaun Watsonâs (starting job) to lose,â Ochocinco said. âSo, theyâre gonna allow him to start, and they had two games on the road. Iâm not sure whatâs gonna happen with those two games, hoping he looks the part. But if he doesnât, that first home game, the third game of the season, if itâs not going well, at that point a change will be made.âHe then made his prediction even more direct.âMark my words, I havenât been wrong yet. â¦ If the third game does not go the way it should, a change will be made going into Week 4. articles.summary: Veteran outside linebacker Haason Reddick is receiving interest from NFL teams amid franchises inking deals with pass-rushers, including the Dallas Cowboys' one-year deal for Von Miller.
articles.body:
Veteran outside linebacker Haason Reddick is receiving interest from NFL teams amid franchises inking deals with pass-rushers, including the Dallas Cowboys' one-year deal for Von Miller.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the latest.

Reddick has played nine NFL seasons for the Arizona Cardinals, Carolina Panthers, Philadelphia Eagles, New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He is a two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro Second Teamer who amassed 50.5 sacks from 2020-2023.

Reddick, who turns 32 on Sept. 22, has not been as productive in recent years. He amassed one sack and three quarterback hits over 10 games on the 2024 Jets and 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hits in 13 games for the 2025 Buccaneers.

Still, there's no denying his talent, and it's certainly possible Reddick can enjoy a resurgence in 2026. Teams reportedly have interest in bringing him aboard, so we'll see if anything comes to fruition before Week 1 of the NFL season, which runs from Sept. 9-14.

When asked if Steve would call plays if he returned, Bill simply said there was âno updateâ and added that he did not want to discuss the medical situation.âYeah, no update,â Bill said. âYeah, not really going to talk about that situation. articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update, Latest on Bengals WR's Status After Apparent Leg Issue at Practice
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase appears to have avoided a serious left leg injury during his team's practice on Tuesday, as he said that he would've been able to continue if needed after suffering a "hyperextension."
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase appears to have avoided a serious left leg injury during his team's practice on Tuesday, as he said that he would've been able to continue if needed after suffering a "hyperextension."

CBS Cincinnati's Yanni Tragellis and NBC 5 Cincinnati's Charlie Clifford provided more information.

The former LSU star has posted a 17-game average of 113 catches, 1,490 yards and 12 touchdowns over his first five seasons (2021-2025), per Pro Football Reference .

Chase enjoyed a career-best 2024 season, winning the receiver triple crown with 127 catches, 1,708 yards and 17 touchdowns, leading pass-catchers in all categories. For his efforts, Chase earned himself a four-year, $161 million contract extension .

Chase was exceptional yet again in 2025, catching 125 passes for 1,412 yards and eight scores. He's put up those numbers despite the team missing superstar quarterback Joe Burrow, who was out nine weeks after suffering a Grade 3 turf toe injury a Week 2 win (31-27) against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

He's missed games due to injury on two separate occasions. In 2022 , Chase suffered a hairline hip fracture that cost him five games. In 2023 , an AC joint sprain forced him out for one game.

Losing the 26-year-old for any period of time would be a massive blow for the Bengals. Cincinnati does have other capable pass-catching talents, namely wide receiver Tee Higgins, who posted 1,000-yard seasons in 2021 and 2022 and caught 10 touchdown passes in 2024. But Chase is one of the game's elite wide receivers at his best. Replacing that superstar talent is impossible. Thankfully, all appears well here.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Picks in 2-Round Mock Draft and Top Keeper Rankings Advice
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.

While your specific league may require you to weigh thinks like draft-round or salary-cap costs, the general goal is keeping as much talent as possible.

It isn't always as simple as it sounds, though, so you might have come here seeking a few road signs to take you to title town. That's exactly what we have here in the form of a two-round mock draft, dynasty rankings and keeper advice.

This might be the most obvious advice you will hear, but it's also the most important. Because each keeper league has its own set of rules, you need to know exactly what they are, so you can apply them to the general advice you'll find in a place like this.

Universal rankings can be helpful, but they may not settle your debates. If your league uses a salary cap or attaches draft-pick costs to keepers, that changes things a lot. That third-round sleeper you found last season may not look as appealing this year if they jump to a second- or even first-round cost, for instance.

If you keep a big chunk of your roster, then you should have a pretty decent idea of your championship chances this season. Use those odds—the realistic ones, not the optimistic ones that only exist in a best-case scenario—to steer your draft decisions.

Win-right-now rosters need instant-impact, so you'd want to prioritize proven veterans over dart-throw rookies. Long-term rebuilders, on the other hand, have no use for 30-somethings, but they should be collecting as many long-term lottery tickets as possible. It only takes one jackpot prize or two to instantly change your team's trajectory.

articles.title: New Giants Rumors Update Calvin Austin III's 'Serious' Knee Injury Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The New York Giants are hoping for the best after a key member of the offense suffered an injury on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are hoping for the best after a key member of the offense suffered an injury on Tuesday.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, wide receiver Calvin Austin suffered a "serious knee injury" and had to be carted off the field during practice.

According to Dan Duggan of The Athletic, Austin was running a route in 1-on-1s when he went down with what appeared to be a right knee injury. Duggan noted that those around Austin "couldn't even look" as he was attended to.

The injury comes ahead of Austin's fifth NFL season, where he was looking to break through as a top option in New York. He spent the first four years of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers before signing with the Giants in March.

Last year, Austin recorded 372 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.

Austin was expected to be the starting slot receiver for the Giants this year, but his injury on Tuesday means New York might have to find someone else to fill that role in the meantime. With Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton starting on the outside, the Giants could pivot to Braxton Berrios in the slot.

With Odell Beckham Jr. still looking for a permanent spot on the Giants, the veteran receiver could be in the mix to take over Austin's role.

Unfortunately for Austin, a significant injury would only add to what has been an injury-filled start to his career. Drafted in the fourth round in 2022, he missed all of his rookie season because of a lingering foot injury that he suffered in training camp.

articles.title: Dolly Partonâs final message to Travis Kelce is breaking hearts after her death
articles.summary: NFL News: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she \"died peacefully today in Nashville\" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, an.
articles.body: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she "died peacefully today in Nashville" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, and no cause of death has been shared yet. And one of her last public moments with Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift is hitting harder now. This one clip, from just weeks ago, where she made a joke about wanting Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's future baby, is doing the rounds for a different reason now.When Dolly Parton joked she wanted Travis Kelce's firstborn, and why that memory now hits so hardBack in early July, Kelce and Swift donated $2 million to Dolly's Imagination Library, as part of a $26 million round of giving to charities tied to cities that mattered to them, announced right before their Madison Square Garden wedding.Dolly didn't just thank them quietly. She filmed a video, saying, "Taylor and Travis, it's Dolly, and I was just told that you two are making a donation of two million dollars to my Imagination Library. Thank you, thank you, thank you," before turning the moment into pure Dolly comedy, joking she wanted their firstborn because "that is gonna be one special baby." Then she sang "I Will Always Love You" straight into the camera, aimed right at them.It was funny then. It's something else entirely now. A woman who spent her whole life turning warmth into a punchline, gifting one more piece of herself to a couple she'd probably never met in person, that's the kind of thing you don't get to see twice.Remembering Dolly, beyond the jokeShe started out singing in church, was on local radio and TV by 13, and made her Grand Ole Opry debut around that same age, where she met Johnny Cash. From there she built one of the great crossover careers in music, releasing dozens of albums and winning 11 Grammys.But the Imagination Library, the same program Kelce and Swift just backed, was always the part of her legacy that felt closest to her heart. It wasn't about the music. It was about kids she'd never meet, getting books they'd never have gotten otherwise.Her family has asked that, instead of flowers, donations go to that same Imagination Library. Fitting, really. Even her goodbye is pointed at the same thing that clip was about - kids, books, and a kind of love that outlasts the person giving it.Kelce and Swift's $2 million didn't just fund a program. It funded a promise Dolly made a long time ago, one she's now handed off for good.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Odell Beckham Jr., Giants Depth Chart Are Impacted by Austin Injury Ahead of Roster Cut Deadline
articles.summary: The New York Giants' receiving corps took a hit after Calvin Austin III suffered an injury in practice on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Giants' receiving corps took a hit after Calvin Austin III suffered an injury in practice on Tuesday.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Austin was carted off the field after a "serious" knee injury.

With the 27-year-old likely set to miss time, the Giants will look further down their depth chart as they attempt to make up for his impact.

This could be beneficial for Odell Beckham Jr.'s chances of making the team, as the veteran is looking to stay in New York beyond Sunday's deadline to trim rosters down to 53 players.

Paul Schwartz of the New York Post also noted that Austin's injury "opens the door" for Beckham to secure a roster spot.

Although Beckham didn't play for any team during the 2025 season, he returned to the squad that he started his career with on a minimum contract in June.

The 33-year-old has been on the Giants' roster bubble throughout training camp, with Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic predicting that he wouldn't make the team on Monday.

While Beckham has occasionally worked with New York's first-team offense, he's spent the majority of camp as a reserve option. Still, he's made several impressive plays in practice.

During his first preseason appearance this year, he caught two passes for six yards. In Beckham's second preseason contest, he hauled in two receptions for 17 yards.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh was particularly impressed with his latest performance.

"I thought he looked pretty good," Harbaugh said, per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . "He made a couple catches. There were some things he could have done better. But he looked solid, I would say. I love Odell. What he's doing, what he's fighting for, I don't know how it's gonna turn out … But to see his fight, his determination, his humility … [I'm] really proud of him."

Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton are New York's established starters at wide receiver, while Malachi Fields was selected with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft. The Giants also brought in Darnell Mooney on a one-year deal worth up to $10 million in March.

Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre, Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins and Jalin Hyatt are among the players competing with Beckham for New York's backup receiver spots.

Sunday's cut-down deadline is at 6 p.m. ET.

Antonio Brown, never one to pass up a free shot at his old quarterback, called the look straight-up a "Terminator villain." articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Ankle Injury Status Discussed by Raiders' Klint Kubiak Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders fans looking for clarity on the severity of Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury didn't get much from head coach Klint Kubiak on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders fans looking for clarity on the severity of Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury didn't get much from head coach Klint Kubiak on Tuesday.

"I'm not gonna get into the injuries," Kubiak told reporters when asked about the running back. "He's on the mend."

He also said , "Ashton got hurt in practice and the whole team took a knee. I think that says a lot about him being on the mend and us counting on him. So, really excited to get him back."

The comments come after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that Jeanty seemed to have avoided a season-ending injury.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

There was significant concern for Jeanty in the immediate aftermath of his setback, especially since Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post reported he couldn't put weight on his leg as he exited the field.

Yet ESPN's Adam Schefter and Rapoport reported it wasn't seen as "a long-term injury" even though there was still some uncertainty regarding the exact timeline.

Considering how secretive some NFL coaches are when it comes to injury updates, Kubiak's comments aren't surprising. He and the Raiders also may not know exactly when the running back will be ready to return to the field at this point.

Las Vegas starts the 2026 campaign on Sept. 13 against the Miami Dolphins.

Jeanty figures to be a major part of its offensive attack after he ran for 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie. The Raiders selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft with the hope he would become a franchise building block, and the 2026 campaign represents a chance for him to take a second-year leap.

He has to be on the field to do that, though, which makes the timing of his setback rather concerning even if it isn't a season-ending one.

If Jeanty is out for the game against the Dolphins, look for the Raiders to turn to Mike Washington Jr. at running back.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes says he feels 'great,' still hoping to play in Week 1
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has apparently hit the most optimistic deadlines during his ACL recovery.
articles.body:
When Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes went down with an ACL injury last December, the quarterback seemed likely to miss time early next season. While a quick ACL recovery wasn't necessarily unprecedented, it was rare.

With a few weeks to go before the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, Mahomes said he feels "great" and is still hopeful he'll be able to start in Week 1.

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7 — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) August 25, 2026

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7

Mahomes said he was initially told it would take nine months to recover from his injury. The quarterback underwent surgery Dec. 16, making Sept. 16 exactly nine months since his surgery. The Chiefs are slated to take on the Denver Broncos in Week 1 on Sept. 14, two days before the actual nine-month mark.

That's an aggressive timeline, but one Mahomes said he was always planning to hit.

"This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

While that's an encouraging update — as is the fact that Mahomes has been able to take part in team practices — the star quarterback has yet to be cleared to play in games just yet. If that doesn't happen by Friday, Mahomes would miss the entire NFL preseason for the first time in his career.

Even in that case, Mahomes would still have two more weeks to be cleared by team doctors.

articles.body:
The Chicago Bears reportedly are discussing moving on from a key defensive player.

Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the team has had trade talks regarding defensive tackle Gervon Dexter and "there are multiple scenarios where a deal could get done sending him to a new team."

The report from Schultz comes after Dexter left Thursday's practice early , which perhaps is an indication that a trade is on the horizon.

It's unclear whether Dexter and the Bears have had contract talks, but it's fair to assume they have considering he's entering the final year of his rookie deal. A potential trade could give Dexter the chance to get more money than he otherwise would have in Chicago.

Dexter, 24, is coming off a season in which he logged a career-high six sacks along with 44 total tackles in 17 games. His continued growth was a bright spot in what was an overall rough year for the Bears' defense, which allowed the fourth-most yards per game (361.8).

It's unclear which teams are eyeing a potential trade for Dexter, but the Bears would seemingly try to get back a player or two in the deal, considering the lack of depth along the defensive line.

Dexter started all 17 games last year, and Chicago would need someone to come in and fill the void that he would leave if he were moved. The Bears added a few players to the defensive line this offseason, but it's fair to say none are starting-caliber players on a team looking to get back to the playoffs.

articles.summary: NFL News: For about twelve hours, Bengals fans lived through the exact nightmare scenario nobody wants three weeks before kickoff. Their $161 million receiver, .
articles.body: For about twelve hours, Bengals fans lived through the exact nightmare scenario nobody wants three weeks before kickoff. Their $161 million receiver, the guy the entire offense runs through, went down on a routine practice rep with no contact, no pileup, just a bad landing, and grabbed his knee as it mattered. In a league where careers and playoff hopes turn on exactly this kind of moment, that clip was enough to send an entire fanbase into a spiral before a single official word came out. Then, just as fast as the panic built, Chase himself picked up a mic and tried to shut it all down. Here's the full arc, from scare to relief, and why it's still worth reading the fine print.JaâMarr Chaseâs scary injury had Bengals fans fearing the worst Chase went up for a deep route against teammate DJ Turner at Tuesday's practice, landed awkwardly, and immediately grabbed his left knee. Video of the moment spread fast, Chase limping, trainers rushing over, head athletic trainer Matt Summers examining him for several minutes on the field.For a team about to open its season, and a receiver who just signed a four-year, $161 million extension in March, that's the kind of clip that sends fanbases spiraling before anyone's said a word officially.Here's the thing, even in the moment, this didn't look like a disaster. Chase walked off under his own power. His limp reportedly eased up as the day went on. He stayed on the practice field afterward instead of heading straight to the locker room, and was seen casually talking with Joe Burrow and DJ Turner not long after. None of that screams "serious injury." But screenshots of a guy grabbing his knee travel faster than context does, so the panic had already set in online before those details caught up.Chase himself is saying it's nothingSpeaking on ESPN 1530 with Tony Pike and Mo Egger, Chase called it a mild hyperextension and said he could have kept playing if it had been a real game. Straight from the source, that's about as reassuring as it gets.That said, worth flagging that this is Chase's own read on his own knee, on a radio hit, not an official Bengals medical statement or an MRI result. Players downplay injuries all the time, sometimes because that's genuinely how it feels, sometimes because nobody wants to hand the rest of the league bulletin-board material before Week 1. The Bengals themselves haven't put out an official statement on severity, so until there's a practice report or a coach's presser confirming Chase is full-go, "hyperextension, no big deal" is Chase's word, not a diagnosis.Best case: this really was a scare and nothing more, and Chase is back to full practice reps within days. Worst case: hyperextensions can still linger even when a guy insists he's fine. Bengals fans have been burned by exactly this pattern before with Chase's past hip and shoulder injuries, where "day-to-day" turned into multiple missed games. articles.title: The fragile, shaky, not-yet-feelgood story of Tua Tagovailoa's next act
articles.summary: Atlanta has two quarterbacks and one big problem: Can either stay healthy?
articles.body:
Walk very gently around the Falcons ' practice fields in Flowery Branch, Georgia. You might injure a quarterback.

Yes, while Cleveland is the site of the most controversial and misbegotten quarterback situation , Atlanta is home to the most delicate. Two oft-injured quarterbacks, Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., are ever-so-carefully competing for the starting job like they're trying to run across a hockey rink.

Penix, who partially tore his ACL last November, finally received clearance to begin full 11-on-11 work on Monday, meaning the Falcons' QB competition can now begin in earnest. Good thing, too, because the regular-season opener is coming up fast, and it's probably a good idea to have a starting QB in place at that point.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

The Falcons snagged Tagovailoa for the NFL equivalent of a scratch-and-dent bargain — one year, $1.2 million — as a combination insurance policy/camp challenge for Penix. This marks a clear new chapter for Tagovailoa, who first came to prominence at Alabama, throwing the famous second-and-26 national championship-winning pass against Georgia in the same building the Falcons call home. After going to Miami in the pandemic draft, where he sported a spectacular suit in his parents' home, Tagovailoa strung together six occasionally transcendent, often maddening injury-pocked seasons.

Tagovailoa occupies a strangely sympathetic position in the modern NFL. No other quarterback has suffered so much, so visibly in this decade, with at least four documented head injuries, along with an assortment of other health woes. A not-insignificant contingent of NFL fandom and commentators has called on Tagovailoa to retire — not because he's hurting the team, which is usually the reason for these calls, but out of fear he's hurting himself and jeopardizing his future.

A newly-released study which states that 25 percent of recently deceased NFL players had CTE is a stark reminder that head trauma remains a concern for NFL players, if not necessarily a headline-worthy news item. And if you're making a list of known head trauma victims now playing in the NFL, well, Tagovailoa tops the list, and there's no close second.

The head injuries alone are enough to proceed with caution on Tagovailoa, but this is a guy who's sustained shots all over his body — back, shoulder, knee, hip, ankle, throwing hand, foot, ribs. Point to a spot between the top of your head and the soles of your feet, and Tagovailoa has probably lost games after injuring it. He's been carted off fields all over the country, wearing both Alabama crimson and Miami teal. Even though he's now in Falcon red-and-black, the questions persist: How much more can he take of this?

For his part, Tagovailoa leans heavily on his faith to guide him through one of the more agonizing journeys in the NFL right now. "Outside of being able to feel centered, it also gives me a lot of perspective on life, what's important in life," he said recently at training camp. "Football is just what we do. It's not who we are."

After missing time early in the preseason with a tight back, Tagovailoa has been taking first-team reps while Penix heals. The results have looked good in practice, not so good in the first preseason game against Denver — 3-for-5 for 22 yards, with just one first down in two offensive series. He's never had a big arm, and he hasn't unleashed it with any regularity in a Falcons uniform, either.

"You have to make use of every opportunity you have, and that's not what we did," Tagovailoa said after the Broncos game, via The Athletic . "Definitely not up to standard. I have to be better for our guys."

"He's getting better every day," Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt insisted recently, per the team's website . "I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and the play-calls and protection adjustments and everything."

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is keeping his cards close on naming a starter, waiting to see how Penix performs in full-squad drills. But as with the ongoing scuffle in Cleveland, the fact that Tagovailoa hasn't yet seized the job for himself is at least a mild indictment in itself. (Tagovailoa did not play in the Falcons' second preseason game; no starters did.)

The Falcons backed themselves into this corner by drafting Penix just weeks after signing now-departed Kirk Cousins , and then watching as both went down with injuries and ineffectiveness. What should have been a position of excessive riches is now one of the largest question marks in the NFL.

For a team that's suffering through the longest playoff drought outside of the Jets — eight years and counting — the Falcons can't afford any more question marks. Atlanta needs answers, and fast. Still undetermined: whether Tagovailoa is the one to provide them.

articles.title: At least 25% of ex-NFL players who died from 2016-2021 had CTE, according to new study; NFLPA says findings should be 'a call to action across the entire football ecosystem'
articles.summary: The study used brain samples from the UNITE Brain Bank at Boston University.
articles.body:
A new study of NFL players who had played in at least one of the league's games and died between 2016-2021 showed at least 25% of them had CTE.

The study from researchers at Mass General Brigham — published Tuesday in The British Medical Journal — deepens the link between the head impacts NFL players suffer and chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the degenerative brain disease known as CTE.

"We've known that this disease process can be caused by, in part, repeated traumatic brain injury. But we didn't know how common it was," said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, lead author of the study, according to NPR .

The study used brain samples from the UNITE Brain Bank at Boston University, where the brains of more than 330 players who died from 2008-2021 have been donated. Researchers tested the brains of 235 of the 878 players who died from 2016-2021 for CTE. They found the disease in 215 of them.

Mood swings, memory loss and confusion are among the symptoms of CTE.

The NFL "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league said in a statement to NPR.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing. We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

In response to the study's release, the NFL Players Association, according to Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio , sent its membership an email Tuesday acknowledging the data:

"These findings should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem. We all share a responsibility to advance research, improve access to care, develop better treatments, and support those affected by the long-term impacts of the game. While we have learned a great deal over the past two decades, there is more work to do."

The study's authors said the 25% estimate is likely low, not accounting for deceased players whose brains were not tested.

The NCAA granted five years of eligibility over the course of five years going forward in a new ruling this offseason but didn't grandfather in athletes who started college during the 2022-23 academic year. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Gives Week 1 Injury Status Update Amid Knee Rehab as Chiefs Prepare for Broncos
articles.summary: There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.

Patrick Mahomes told reporters Tuesday he feels like he is on track to start in Week 1 as he continues his recovery from the torn ACL and LCL that ended his 2025 season.

"Being able to go out there, day after day, and have the grind of a camp, that can even be harder than the [regular] season," Mahomes said. "It's been awesome for me to be able to do that. It's exciting. I didn't know if I was going to have to take days off, but my body has responded the right way.

"Honestly, the more we practice, the better I feel."

While he has not played in a preseason game and is not expected to in Friday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, Mahomes has not missed practice since he was cleared to participate in football activities in July.

And, in his eyes, the timeline is matching up exactly as he expected.

"It's nine months," Mahomes said of the Week 1 start date. "It's the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week 1. I'm someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right.

"This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

This will be the first time in Mahomes' career that he doesn't play in a single preseason game, but the Chiefs know what they are getting in their star quarterback if he is healthy and available.

His resume includes three Super Bowl titles, three Super Bowl MVPs, two league MVPs, six Pro Bowl selections and six seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards. He led the league in both passing yards (5,250) and passing touchdowns (41) in 2022 and is already considered one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history.

It seems like he will have the opportunity to add to that resume this season given his progress from last year's injury.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan breaks 49ers silence on Jed York arrest, says he still has 'respect' for the club owner
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan says Jed York's arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting has no effect on the San Francisco 49ers as a team heading into the season.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers said they weren't going to comment about owner Jed York getting caught up in a prostitution sting over the weekend because the legal matter is closed , but that policy collapsed in coach Kyle Shanahan's first press conference since the incident. Shanahan became the first 49ers official to face questions, and he felt obliged to provide answers. (Dude is a saint). Shanahan said York's arrest and ensuing no-contest plea to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools charges in a deal with an Ohio prosecutor has no effect on the Bay Area football team. MORE DETAILS EMERGE ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN PROSTITUTION STING "My view is, as the coach, does it have effect on us as a team?" Shanahan said. "And that's what I continue to answer on from a football standpoint. It has no effect on us. I mean, as far as what we do day to day, what we talk about, it hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today. It doesn't have to do with what happens on the field." Shanahan, who was involved in a head-on collision in July that affected how much he was on the field early in training camp, doesn't believe that or York's legal trouble will distract the football team in the upcoming season. "Well, the one thing that went on yesterday I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team. "So I think it's been training camp as usual." 49ERS COACH KYLE SHANAHAN ADMITS HE CAUSED CAR CRASH AFTER TAKING EYES OFF ROAD TO FIND HIS PHONE This, of course, is a head coach's spin on an uncomfortable situation. The majority owner of the team spent a day in jail and was splashed across national headlines because, police documents say, he went on a website in Ohio and tried to enlist the services of a prostitute on Sunday. Three times. And he got caught because what he was actually doing was connecting with an operation run by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which arrested him with the help of East Palestine police. NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK Despite those details, Shanahan said he has not changed his opinion about the club's owner or his family. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan admitted after saying he has spoken to York the last two days. "I mean, the views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. "But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it being a personal [matter], I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way." Danielle Belluomini is York's wife of 15 years, but even the marriage has become a newsworthy drama. Multiple reports have cited a divorce petition filed by York almost four months ago with the reason for the break being "irreconcilable differences." NFL owners are scheduled to gather on Wednesday to vote on the sale of the Seattle Seahawks and the York situation will almost definitely be discussed in some capacity. The league released a statement on Monday saying it is aware of York's situation, and he is subject to discipline under its Personal Conduct Policy. So, whether Shanahan admits it or not, the football team could be affected if York is disciplined and that rises to a suspension or even removal — the latter of which is not likely but cannot be ruled out. "That's what these guys deal with their whole careers," Shanahan said. "I got cameras on all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games, when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened. "I feel something like this is actually easier for them than some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle of things that are more personal to themselves." articles.summary: With another Super Bowl on the horizon, the Las Vegas Raiders want to elevate its premier sports venue with a new multi-level event space aimed at tackling h...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are seeking approval for a $158 million upgrade to Allegiant Stadium 's north entrance, including $75 million in public funding. The proposal would add a larger arrival area with pedestrian and event decks, a public plaza, and transportation improvements around the stadium.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority considered the proposal at its August 20 meeting but did not vote on it. A vote could come September 2, with construction expected to begin after the Raiders' 2026 season. The project is being planned for completion in late 2028 or before the 2029 Super Bowl, which is scheduled to be held at Allegiant Stadium. NFL.com has more details on the proposal and funding plan .

New North Entrance Would Change the Arrival Experience

The proposed project centers on the north side of Allegiant Stadium, where large crowds currently converge after Raiders games and other major events.

The plans include an elevated pedestrian deck, an event deck, a public plaza and improvements to traffic and transportation access. A dedicated rideshare loop would sit beneath the second level, with the goal of making pickups and drop-offs more efficient.

Related: Popular rock band makes major change to Las Vegas Sphere residency

The new entrance would also provide a more direct connection from the Las Vegas Strip, with many fans currently using the nearby Hacienda Avenue bridge to reach the stadium.

Raiders president Sandra Douglass Morgan told the Stadium Authority that the north side has become a pressure point for the guest experience because the existing infrastructure is stretched to capacity.

How the $158 Million Project Would Be Funded

The Raiders are proposing that the Stadium Authority contribute up to $75 million, with the remaining cost covered by the team. The public portion would come from the waterfall residual fund, which is funded by room tax revenue.

The stadium itself opened in 2020 at a reported construction cost of about $2 billion. Public funding contributed to the original project totaled approximately $750 million.

The proposed improvements are intended to prepare the venue for the larger crowds and logistical demands that come with major sporting events and concerts. Allegiant Stadium hosted Super Bowl LVIII in 2024, and the venue is scheduled to host the 2028 Final Four as well as the 2029 Super Bowl.

For now, the project remains a proposal. The Stadium Authority did not take action on August 20, leaving a potential September 2 vote as the next major step.

The Raiders want construction to begin after the 2026 season, with completion targeted for late 2028 or earlier. A successful project would give one of Las Vegas' most prominent sports venues a significantly larger arrival area before it takes on another Super Bowl.

articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest
articles.summary: York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges, disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools, was sentenced to two days in jail and fined $1,150.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used the pseudonym "Joe" while responding to a fictitious ad on a prostitution website, leading to his Sunday morning arrest in a mobile home park located in East Palestine, Ohio, according to a Tuesday report from The Athletic .

York was charged with a pair of misdemeanors, initially including a prostitution charge that was eventually amended to disorderly conduct through a plea agreement, per ESPN . York's other charge was reportedly for possession of criminal tools, a classification that can apply to a cell phone. He pleaded no contest, was sentenced to two days in jail, one for each charge, and fined $1,150.

The Athletic, citing an incident report from the Mahoning Valley Law Enforcement Task Force, reported that police deployed an undercover advertisement, masquerading as a woman, to arrange a meeting with the 46-year-old York, who reportedly filed for divorce from his wife in May.

York contacted what he didn't know was an undercover officer twice on Saturday, according to ESPN , which also cited the incident report. The undercover officer reportedly didn't respond to York until Sunday, when York sent a third message.

York, a Youngstown, Ohio, native, messaged at 9:11 a.m. ET that he was driving in from nearby Boardman, per The Athletic. The two sides reportedly agreed on one hour of "full service sexual activity" for $160, and York was provided a fake lot number in East Palestine mobile home park, identified as the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in ESPN's report.

As reported by The Athletic, York was seen driving a rental car into the mobile home park and then back out to the main road after he couldn't find the made-up lot number. That's where he was reportedly stopped by police, who took York's phone and the $160 he planned to pay. That money was ultimately forfeited to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, according to The Athletic's report, but York's phone was returned.

York was named the 49ers' CEO in 2008. That's when he assumed day-to-day control of the team from his parents. In 2024, he purchased enough equity from his family to take over as the organization's principal owner.

Under York's supervision, San Francisco has reached the Super Bowl three times, although the franchise is still searching for its first ring since the 1994 season.

"As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the 49ers said in a statement regarding York's arrest.

The incident will be reviewed under the NFL's personal conduct policy, a league spokesperson said in a statement, according to multiple outlets.

Notably, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft didn't face punishment from the NFL after he was accused of paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. However, the charges against Kraft, misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution, were dropped.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Honored by Sports World After Country Music Legend Dies at 80
articles.summary: The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.

Dolly Parton died at 80, her nephew, Bryan Seaver, announced on Instagram.

Following Parton's death, the sports world honored the singer, whose impact stretched well beyond just her music.

Parton's music career spanned nearly 60 years, and she is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, with hits like "I Will Always Love You," "9-5" and "Jolene."

She was born in Sevier County, Tennessee, and went on to become arguably the most famous East Tennessean. She released her first album, "Hello, I'm Dolly," in 1967 and released 48 more solo studio albums, her final being "Rockstar" in 2023.

But Parton's music was just a portion of her extraordinary life.

She opened the Dollywood theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, in 1986, and the park has since become one of the most visited theme parks in the country. As part of the Dollywood Company, she also opened other attractions in the area, like the Dream More Resort and Spa and Dolly Parton's Stampede.

While her philanthropic efforts are immeasurable, Parton's Imagination Library is perhaps the most notable. The program began gifting free books to children in East Tennessee but has since stretched worldwide. Approximately one in six children under the age of five in the United States receives an Imagination Library Book each year.

Parton was a lifelong Tennessee fan and appeared at the Vols' 2023 game against Georgia to perform "Rocky Top," escorted onto the field by legendary quarterback Peyton Manning.

Parton had revealed on social media over the past year that her health began declining in March 2025 following the death of her husband, Carl Dean, with the most recent update coming last week.

articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Texted Woman He Believed Was a Prostitute Before His Arrest in Police Sting
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.

The report from the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force had more than two pages redacted but provided more details about what led to York's arrest and ultimately to him pleading no contest Monday to two misdemeanors.

York initially responded to an advertisement placed by police on a known prostitution website on Saturday, according to the report, sending two messages that went unanswered and saying his name was "Joe" and that he wanted to visit the woman.

49ers Owner Pleads No Contest to Misdemeanor Charges (AP)

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

York texted again Sunday morning and said he wanted to see the woman. He said he was staying nearby and asked for her address. He asked how much the woman charged and was told it was $160 for "full service sexual activity," the report said.

York took a rental car to a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio, where he was given a fictitious lot number. He texted when he arrived at the mobile home park. He was then directed back to the main road, where he was stopped by marked police units. Police found York had $160 that was seized and they sent a text to his phone to determine it was the same one used to arrange the meeting.

He was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest Monday to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the ad.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. The $160 that was seized from him was given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.

York has been in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown, for most of the summer. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league is aware of the arrest and will review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the policy.

The team said that the "legal matter" had been resolved and that it would have no additional comment.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that he has talked to York the past two days and doesn't believe the arrest will have any impact on the team.

"Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan said. "The views for the organization going forward are the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got lot of respect for Danielle. The family does mean a lot to me. With it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way."

Shanahan said he doesn't expect any change in York's involvement with the team, saying he has always allowed Shanahan and general manager John Lynch to make the football decisions.

Shanahan said he doesn't feel the need to address the situation with his players.

Star linebacker Fred Warner said the players were aware of it but that he didn't believe it would be a distraction.

"We all have social media, so we see things," he said. "But at the same time, I got a lot of love, a lot respect for Jed, and don't feel the need to comment on the situation. I think the team is kind of the same way. It really wasn't a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but at the time, we were so hyper-focused in this building of trying to prepare for Week 1. A lot of guys are on the bubble trying to make the team. So we're just trying to get better as a football team and that's a personal situation, and letting it stay personal with him."

articles.body: The NFL continues to make a concerted effort for safe play for all players, especially when it comes to head injuries. But since chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, was found to be heavily linked to former professional football players, there has been ongoing discussion about how current and future NFL players could be affected. For the study, 878 former NFL players who died from 2016-21, which varied from players in their 20s to their 80s and in between, at least 215 of them had CTE in some stage. That’s 24.5%, with the actual prevalence likely being higher considering there were 643 of those brains that were not examined. One of the main problems of the degenerative brain disease is that it can only be confirmed as a diagnosis post-death once the brain is examined. The neurodegenerative disease is caused by repeated blows to the head as well as severe head trauma. The symptoms found in those with CTE include memory loss, mood swings, erratic behavioral actions and more. While the disease was first found in boxers, it has become associated with football players in this modern era due to the repeated blows to the head sustained on every snap of the ball. It has, however, also been found in athletes participating in hockey, rugby and other sports. But its connection to football became public when beloved players like Junior Seau, Mike Webster, Frank Gifford and others were diagnosed with CTE after their deaths. Dr. Julian Bailes, a neurosurgeon and chief medical advisor for Q-30 Sports Science, has spent decades studying the disease as well as concussion and repetitive subconcussive impacts. He helped pioneer the early investigation into CTE, being portrayed by Alec Baldwin in the popular film, "Concussion." He has also authored more than 300 publications and previously advised the NFL Players Association, NCAA and Pop Warner Football. Seeing this study, Dr. Bailes believes it "should be a call to action for everyone involved in football." SUPER BOWL CHAMPION STEVE MCMICHAEL, WHO DIED LAST YEAR, REVEALED TO HAVE CTE "We have made tremendous progress in recognizing and managing concussions, but the science increasingly tells us that diagnosed concussions are only part of the equation," Dr. Bailes said in a statement provided to OutKick. "Repetitive head impacts accumulated over years of play matter, and we need to bring the same urgency we’ve applied to understanding CTE to preventing and reducing the forces experienced by the brain in the first place. "That means continuing to advance rules, training, equipment and new approaches to brain protection at every level of the game. This should not be approached as an all or nothing assignment. The next frontier in athlete safety must be proactive brain protection." A simple proactive action would be eliminating repeated blows to the head, which researchers know prevents CTE. Obviously, the game of football would forever be changed and there’s much more complexities there, especially at the professional level. "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league told The Athletic in a statement. The Big Ten announced a ruling Tuesday morning that would ban players returning from the NFL to play for a Big Ten school.

The ruling comes after Dae'Quan Wright, a tight end for the Cleveland Browns , announced his intentions to leave the NFL and join his previous head coach from a year ago, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

While college basketball has seen its fair share of similar instances, this was the first case in college football, with many more likely to pursue the option to return to college.

Although the Big Ten has been the first conference to ban former NFL players from playing in their conference, there is an expectation that the SEC will have similar talks regarding a ruling.

Following comments made by Bret Bielema last week, this could have notable repercussions for Illinois.

Former Illini wide receiver Hank Beatty and offensive lineman Melvin Priestly were prime candidates to return prior to the ruling.

Bielema had mentioned an interest in recruiting them to return to Illinois if both were eligible.

Both would have been great additions to the roster this fall, but as it stands, the Illinois roster appears to be set ahead of its season opener on September 3rd against UAB.

At a time when college athletics is akin to the Wild West, a ruling such as this provides a rare win for the NCAA to create a more stable league.

articles.title: UCLA suggests star transfer Trent Hendrick isn't impacted by new Big Ten NFL player ban
articles.summary: UCLA athletics director Martin Jarmond released a statement that school is complying with all Big Ten rules and all players on its roster are eligible.
articles.body:
UCLA is proceeding as though it landed a massive gift this week, with 2025 Sun Belt player of the year Trent Hendrick joining the Bruins for practices Monday and Tuesday.

Hendrick is among 16 players who sought a Louisiana temporary restraining order allowing them to return to college after entering the NFL draft pool, arguing they would not have left had they know NCAA rules would change granting them an extra year of eligibility.

The temporary restraining order was granted last week, but the Big Ten voted on Tuesday to pass a new rule that prohibited football players who have signed a professional contract, were on a professional roster at any point or declared for the NFL draft as an underclassman without withdrawing, from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition.

Hendrick went undrafted and participated in rookie minicamps with the Cleveland Browns and Kansas City Chiefs , but the linebacker never signed with a team and didn't leave school early to enter the NFL draft.

He also never earned a spot on a roster.

"We support the Big Ten's adoption of the new professional football players rule and understand the importance of having clear and consistent eligibility standards across the conference," UCLA athletic director Martin Jarmond said in a statement on Tuesday. "We have been in communication with the Big Ten throughout this process, and our student-athletes are eligible under the guidelines adopted today. We are excited to turn our full attention to the upcoming season and our opener [versus] California on Sept. 5."

It is unclear whether anyone will contest the Louisiana temporary restraining order.

For now, Hendrick is quickly getting up to speed in a system he learned while competing under head coach Bob Chesney and defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler last season at James Madison.

Chesney was excited on Monday to welcome Hendrick to Westwood. Hitschler told reporters Tuesday he, too, was pleased to see Hendrick on the UCLA roster.

"We had a lot of fun together last year and I think he did a great job where he was," Hitschler said. "I'm glad he got the opportunity for himself to hopefully continue to play college football here. What a special opportunity for him and let's make the most of it."

Both coaches said they faced competition to land Hendrick after last week's restraining order was granted.

"He's a really good player," Hitschler said. "He made a lot of plays for us last year and he loves the game. ... Awesome kid, loves the game, loves the work, loves the grind, you know, and he's talented."

Can a player who joined a roster less than two weeks before the season opener be ready to play immediately? Hitschler thinks so.

"Trent's a kid that stays ready," Hitschler said. "He was begging for an opportunity to get a tryout in the league. Just another opportunity to maybe get it. So he was working out, he was in great shape. He's a kid that lives, eats and sleeps football and God blessed him with an opportunity here, let's see what he can make of it."

The Big Ten is holding schools accountable for compliance with its rule and told the Associated Press restrictions in other sports such as basketball could follow.

A head football coach who plays a former pro will be suspended 50% of the season and his school will be fined, the Big Ten confirmed to the AP on Tuesday.

The topic is a hot one around college athletics. Wake Forest athletic director John Currie, chairman of the Atlantic Coast Conference athletic directors group for the upcoming season, said his colleagues planned to discuss the issue Wednesday.

"I don't think anybody in our league likes the idea of taking away opportunities from existing college students and graduating high school players, which is exactly what is happening when a school signs a player out of an NFL camp to their team," Currie wrote in a text message to the AP.

Duke coach Manny Diaz said the Power Four conferences need to present a unified front. The Southeastern Conference passed a rule later Tuesday banning players who have been drafted by NFL, NBA or WNBA teams or listed on rosters in those leagues.

"I think you'll see more leagues start to govern themselves since we're having such a hard time finding it at a national level," Diaz said. "I think everyone understands it's absolutely absurd. We can enjoy the fact that the players can benefit financially from playing in college now. At the same time, recognize the ultimate truth that we're not a professional sports franchise. We are a collegiate, scholastic school activity, and we've got to rein that in."

Agent Drew Rosenhaus told the AP on Monday that former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright had been waived by the Cleveland Browns and, if he clears waivers, will join Lane Kiffin's roster at Louisiana State. Wright played two seasons for Kiffin at Ole Miss.

Wright was among a group of players who sued in a Louisiana court, saying the new NCAA rule granting five years of eligibility to most athletes should apply to him and others who were not "grandfathered" into the rule, which did not include the high school Class of 2022.

"Over 100 athletes in multiple sports were cleared and said you could go play. That's a court order," Kiffin said Tuesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" on ESPN. "If you think back on all the different court orders of great players that were granted — whether that's Diego Pavia or, now, Trinidad [Chambliss] that were allowed to play a sixth year, we followed all court orders. I think you get into a really interesting situation as a conference if you're now saying, 'Well, we're not going to follow this court order.' These kids that a court says can go anywhere, we're going to say, 'No you can't.'"

The situation has drawn sharp criticism among coaches in college and the NFL. Rams coach Sean McVay said reversing the college football-to-NFL pipeline was mind-boggling.

"I don't know enough about it, other than the fact guys that can be in NFL camps, if it doesn't go down for them, they can go back to college," McVay said. "I mean, I feel like I took a freaking gummy. I don't even understand it. It's true. I mean, looking at this stuff, I'm like, surely that's not real. But I just try to stay in my lane. But I would say it's very unique and it's very different."

Correspondent Jordan Puente and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is arguably the most scrutinized quarterback in the NFL today. Three Super Bowl rings, a contract worth a quarter-billion dollars, and a fanbase that tracks his every move. That kind of attention does not come without a cost. Over the past several years, Brittany Mahomes has become far more than a supportive presence in the stands. She has quietly shaped the environment that allows her husband to stay locked in, week after week, at the highest level of the sport.How does Brittany Mahomes support Patrick Mahomes off the field?The short answer is that she handles everything the spotlight does not show. When Mahomes suffered a high-ankle sprain during the 2023 playoffs and gutted through two more postseason games on a compromised foot, Brittany was not just sitting courtside in his Chiefs jersey. She was managing the household, keeping their two children shielded from the noise, and making sure that when Patrick came home, home actually felt like a refuge.That matters more than people realize. NFL quarterbacks operate on brutal schedules. Film sessions start before sunrise. Road trips eat up weekends. Contract negotiations bleed into training camp. Mahomes has spoken about how family stability directly feeds his focus. "She handles so much so I can focus on football," he said in a 2023 interview. "She keeps everything together."Brittany Mahomes has also been vocal about her role on a public stage that she did not always ask for. When criticism came her way during the Chiefs' championship run, particularly the social media noise around her courtside reactions and public appearances, she did not retreat. She addressed it head-on. That directness, for better or worse, has actually protected her husband. It deflects pressure away from Patrick by drawing some of it toward herself.She launched her own fitness company, pushed her own public identity, and built a life that does not revolve entirely around being Patrick's wife. That distinction matters inside an NFL marriage. Players who come home to partners with their own purpose tend to handle fame differently than those who don't.What role does Brittany Mahomes play in Patrick's mental focus during the season?NFL success is not purely physical. Ask any coach who has managed a top quarterback through adversity, and they will tell you that the mental load is what breaks most players. Mahomes has a rare ability to stay composed under pressure, and Brittany's consistency off the field is part of what anchors that.She has created a home structure that keeps their kids, Sterling and Bronze, grounded and away from the circus that follows their father's name. Mahomes has said repeatedly that seeing his children stay normal keeps him grounded too. That is not an accident. It is a deliberate choice Brittany makes every single week.Their relationship has also weathered real public scrutiny. articles.title: SEC announces ban for former pros: Does this make Mark Mitchell ineligible?
articles.summary: Mark Mitchell committed to Kentucky, but it just got more difficult for him to actually suit up for the Wildcats.
articles.body:
The SEC is joining the Big Ten in prohibiting players who have moved on to professional sports from returning to play college sports at an SEC school.

On Tuesday, the league announced new bylaws to prevent professional players from returning to school.

Going forward, SEC schools are not permitted to have an athlete on a roster who has:

Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Draft, and did not appropriately withdraw,

Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team, or

Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate roster).

SEC commissioner Greg Sankey is also now authorized to enforce this expectation with penalties against member institutions.

Further, here is what else the SEC had to say:

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference," the SEC's statement read. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition."

So, what does this mean for Kentucky? It certainly makes it harder for guys like Mark Mitchell to play this season. Mitchell technically declared for the NBA Draft and agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract so he could play in the NBA Summer League for the Denver Nuggets. But at the time, he was effectively forced to do so since his eligibility clock was up.

A Louisville judge recently ruled that Mitchell is eligible for a fifth season of college basketball . Will that ruling hold up against these new SEC bylaws?

That remains to be seen, but one thing is for sure: These new rules implemented by the SEC just made it more difficult for Mitchell and other class of 2022 players to play one more season. It's unclear if these new bylaws mean Mitchell is now ineligible for next season, though the safe bet would be that, as of right now, he would not be allowed to play in games.

One thing Kentucky and Mitchell do have going for them is there's still plenty of time before the season tips off. They're definitely going to need several more weeks at the very least to get this all sorted out and, hopefully, have a final decision made whether Mitchell can play this season.

Expect more lawsuits to be filed and the fight to continue for those 2022 players to get one more season.

articles.title: How bad is the NFL's CTE problem? A new study just answered that and it's grim
articles.summary: NFL News: A study published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal has put a number to what many in football have long feared. At least one in four NFL players .
articles.body: A study published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal has put a number to what many in football have long feared. At least one in four NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the degenerative brain disease better known as CTE. The research, led by scientists from Harvard Medical School, Massachusetts General Hospital, and Boston University, focused on 878 former NFL players who died in that six-year period. Of that group, at least 215 of them, or 24.5 percent, had CTE. And here is the part that should make the NFL uncomfortable: researchers say that 25 percent figure is likely the floor, not the ceiling.What does the new CTE study actually say about NFL players?The estimate of 25 percent is on the "low end," said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, the study's lead author. The study found that the maximum possible prevalence of CTE was around 97 percent, but the true rate "is somewhere in the middle," Daneshvar said.That range between 25 and 97 percent sounds staggeringly wide, but it reflects a core limitation of CTE research: the disease can only be confirmed in dead tissue. CTE can be diagnosed only after death, so most research has depended on brains donated by players or their families. Of the 878 players in the sample, only 338 actually had their brains examined. The remaining 643 were never studied. Daneshvar's team ran statistical models to estimate what that missing data might look like, which is why the range is so broad.Jesse Mez, a BU CTE Center codirector of clinical research, put it plainly: "If at least 25 percent of NFL players who died had these changes in their brain, then this seems like a call to action for more discussion about risk, more research, and more support for affected families."When applied to active players, that would mean about 400 of the current 1,696 active players could develop CTE. That is not a projection the NFL or the NFLPA can easily dismiss. The NFLPA said in a statement: "This study is a sobering reminder that football carries real risks, and those risks can have lasting consequences for players and their families. The findings should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem."Does the NFL's kickoff rule change make the CTE problem worse?The timing of this study lands in the middle of a live debate inside the league. When the touchback changed to the 35 and teams became incentivized to put more kickoffs in play, concussions spiked. Specifically for the player returning the kick and the player tackling him.That matters because the new BMJ study adds statistical pressure to what some team officials have already been saying privately. As one source put it, it was "the elephant in the room" at the annual league meetings in March. Moving the touchback line from the 30 to the 35 brought more returns, more collisions, and more concussions. Those concussions, accumulated over careers, are precisely what researchers link to CTE development.There is now a camp inside the league that wants the touchback point moved back to the 30. The new study will cause the opponents of the 35-yard touchback point to argue even more loudly that it should return to the 30.There is also an important caveat worth noting. The average age of the former players whose brains were donated was around 66 years old, meaning most of their professional football careers took place before 2005, when CTE was first diagnosed in a former NFL player. One researcher noted this "may not represent the NFL in 2026," given the rule changes and safety improvements made since then. That is a reasonable qualifier. But it does not make the numbers disappear.The NFL has spent years managing this conversation carefully. This study, peer-reviewed and published in one of medicine's most respected journals, makes that harder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
